title: Grateful Dead Live at Crystal Ballroom on 1968-02-03

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard capture of a high‑energy early‑68 set, highlighted by a smoking The Other One suite, New Potato (Schoolgirl), It Hurts Me Too blues leads and an incendiary Eleven.
ai_review.review: The Miller SBD cleanup delivers excellent clarity with only a faint hiss, letting the band’s tight yet adventurous playing shine. Standout moments include the debut‑lyric “The Other One” segue into a superb Cryptical reprise, a stellar New Potato (Schoolgirl) with Pigpen’s harmonica, blistering blues leads on It Hurts Me Too and an electrifying Eleven that bursts into feedback. Overall the performance is rated as one of the better shows of this era.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews are 5‑star, praising both musical performance and recording quality; only a few moderate scores mention minor tape cuts or hiss, yielding a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Charlie Miller’s cleanup yields a crisp mix with minimal hiss; some reviewers note tiny gaps or a faint hiss but no major drop‑outs.

standout_songs: The Other One (suite with debut lyrics)
show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong first half flowing into a seamless second set; The Other One transitions into Cryptical, leading into New Potato and culminating in an explosive Eleven/feedback finish.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for sick blues leads on It Hurts Me Too and jazzy jams during Caboose/China/Eleven; his tone described as superb.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for a cool bass ending on Born Cross‑Eyed ("cool Phil ending").
